subject: WHEN-COMPILED function
notes: cite.py --check 15.99.2 "WHEN-COMPILED" => OK §15.99.2 (General format), rendering exactly `FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED` with both words underlined and NO parenthesised part at all; cite.py --check 15.99.1 "The type of this function is alphanumeric." => OK. THE FORMAT IS DECLARED AND ENFORCED. IntrinsicCatalog.cs:170 carries `Add(new("WHEN-COMPILED", IntrinsicType.Alphanumeric, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 0, 0, "", "WhenCompiled", IntrinsicBind.Fold, false, 85))` - Fixed arity with MinArgs=MaxArgs=0 and an EMPTY ArgKinds string, which is the format diagram transcribed. FOUR REFERENCE SHAPES TRACED, all in Binding/Procedure/Verbs/IntrinsicBinder.cs: (a) `FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED` with no suffix - BindIntrinsic reaches BindIntrinsicCore with an empty argument list and the arity gate at line 573 passes (0 in 0..0); (b) `FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED(x)` - the same gate reports COBOL1504 "FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED takes 0 argument(s); 1 given (ISO §15.3)" and returns BoundExprError, so an argument list is rejected rather than ignored; (c) the keyword-omitted bare name (§8.4.3.2.3 SR2) - KeywordOmittedFunction line 339 admits a bare catalogued name only when `sig.MinArgs == 0`, which WHEN-COMPILED satisfies (the comment at line 335 names it explicitly alongside CURRENT-DATE/PI/E), gated on REPOSITORY declaring the function; (d) `FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED (1:4)` - a depth-0 colon in the captured group routes to ResultRefMod (§8.4.3.3.3 SR2, result reference modification) instead of being read as an argument list, and DefinitionPermitsArguments (line 109, `sig.MaxArgs > 0`) is false so the SR6 arm cannot misfire. The §15.3 class screen agrees with the catalog: IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:722 `["WHEN-COMPILED"] = Uniform(' ', "§15.99.2 - no arguments")`, present (per the comment at line 715) so the drift test holds the table and the catalog in agreement. TEST: IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.WhenCompiled_CompileTimeConstant_PinnedToSpec (tests/WiseOwl.Cobol.Tests.Conformance/IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs:294-303) is spec-pinned, not a legacy differential - it calls AssertSpec (compile + run under WiseOwlCobolCompiler and Assert.Equal on the expected output), never AssertSameAsLegacy - and writes `MOVE FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED TO T` plus `IF FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE >= FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED`, so the keyword form with no argument list is exercised in both a MOVE sending field and a relation-condition operand. WHAT IS MISSING (does not change the verdict): the NEGATIVE half - COBOL1504 on `FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED(1)` - is implemented and read but has no negative-corpus fixture pinning it, and the keyword-omitted leg (2002+, REPOSITORY) is pinned for CURRENT-DATE (golden 2023/pb62_all_subscript_runtime_ranges) but not for WHEN-COMPILED. EDITIONS: no §15.99 edition delta - Annex E carries no WHEN-COMPILED entry and the §15.6 function table row (spec line 30004) shows no version marker, so the batch default stands; the catalog's own IntroducedIn=85 was NOT used to derive this. REFUTED: verdict UPHELD at CONFORMS, code-location CORRECTED. Citation re-derived independently: cite.py --check 15.99.2 "WHEN-COMPILED" => OK §15.99.2 (General format), the diagram being exactly `FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED` with both words underlined and NO parenthesised part; cite.py --check 15.99.3 "The character positions returned, numbered from left to right, are" / "The returned value is the date and time of compilation of the compilation unit that contains this function" / "shall denote the same time as the compilation date and time" => OK §15.99.3 1) / 2) / 3). CODE-LOCATION MOVED from IntrinsicCatalog.cs#IntrinsicCatalog to IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsicCore: the catalog row is DATA (name, 0..0, empty ArgKinds) and enforces nothing; the site that makes the compiler CONFORM to the format is the binder's arity gate, and rule 7 wants the ONE path that implements the rule. I re-walked BindIntrinsicCore line by line to be sure the gate is actually reached for this row rather than diverted: the eight bespoke early returns above it (CONVERT, MODULE-NAME, LENGTH/BYTE-LENGTH, NUMVAL-C, EXCEPTION-FILE, the LOCALE-phrase case arm, STANDARD-COMPARE, TRIM/FIND-STRING/SUBSTITUTE) all key on sig.Name or on ArgKinds, and `sig.ArgKinds.EndsWith('l')` on the EMPTY string is false, so WHEN-COMPILED falls through to BindIntrinsicArgs + the `given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs` gate. THREE ATTACKS RUN AND ALL FAILED, which is why the verdict stands: (1) TWO-ARM DISPATCH on the >>COBOL-WORDS synonym — DefinitionPermitsArguments resolves ctx.CobolWords.Synonyms at line 105, so I checked whether the OTHER arm does; BindIntrinsicCore line 447 resolves the same map before the catalog lookup, so `FUNCTION <synonym>` and the SR6 pre-check agree and there is no drift. (2) THE EMPTY-PARENTHESIS FORM `FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED ()`, which §15.99.2's own diagram does not draw and which the adjudicator never considered: it is nonetheless LEGAL, because §8.4.3.2.2's function-identifier format makes the whole parenthesised part optional AND argument-1 inside it optional (its figure note: 'the whole parenthesized argument list is optional'), and §8.4.3.2.3 SR6's NOTE writes `FUNCTION RANDOM ()` as the argument-less spelling; the compiler accepts it (0 in 0..0) — correct, not a gap. (3) RESERVED-WORD ROUTING: §8.11 (spec line 9711) lists WHEN-COMPILED as an INTRINSIC FUNCTION NAME, not a §8.9 reserved word, so the bare form really does arrive as a dataReference and KeywordOmittedFunction (MinArgs==0 admission at line 339, DialectLevel<2002 routing gate at line 227) is the right arm to have read. TEST-REF UPHELD: AssertSpec (lines 26-31) is `new WiseOwlCobolCompiler(dialect).CompileAndRun(source)` + Assert.Equal on the expected output — no DifferentialGolden, no AssertSameAsLegacy — so it qualifies under rule 3.
